question: Can the Commission say what political, institutional and administrative discussions, if any, have taken place in relation to infringement procedure INFR (2026)4004, and could it clarify the nature of the arguments and opinions put forward by representatives of the Italian State?

Specifically, has the Italian State cited political expediency, budgetary constraints or a desire to curb spending in support of its stance? If this is indeed the case, to what extent (if at all) will the Commission take these arguments into account when assessing the compatibility with EU law of Italy’s regulations governing the economic, welfare and social rights of the tax judges concerned?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.10.2026) On 4 February 2025, the Commission sent the Italian authorities a letter in the framework of pre-infringement dialogue DLGE(2024)10804. The Italian authorities replied on 15 April 2025.

As the explanations provided by the Italian authorities did not adequately address the Commission’s concerns regarding compliance with EU law, on 4 June 2026 the Commission decided to open infringement procedure INFR(2026)4004 by sending Italy a letter of formal notice. The Italian authorities replied to the letter of formal notice on 28 July 2026.
The Commission is currently assessing the Italian authorities’ reply.

As the exchange with Italy in the context of the infringement procedure is still ongoing, the Commission cannot disclose details concerning the arguments put forward by the Italian authorities, as such disclosure could undermine the relationship of mutual trust between the Commission and the Member State concerned and the ongoing dialogue between them.
The Commission will take a position on the appropriate follow-up to the infringement procedure once it has completed its assessment of the Italian authorities’ reply.
